long ccsd_tengy_gpu(const double * __restrict__ f1n,    const double * __restrict__ f1t,
                    const double * __restrict__ f2n,    const double * __restrict__ f2t,
                    const double * __restrict__ f3n,    const double * __restrict__ f3t,
                    const double * __restrict__ f4n,    const double * __restrict__ f4t,
                    const double * __restrict__ dintc1, const double * __restrict__ dintx1, const double * __restrict__ t1v1,
                    const double * __restrict__ dintc2, const double * __restrict__ dintx2, const double * __restrict__ t1v2,
                    const double * __restrict__ eorb,   const double eaijk,
                    double * __restrict__ emp4i, double * __restrict__ emp5i,
                    double * __restrict__ emp4k, double * __restrict__ emp5k,
                    const int ncor, const int nocc, const int nvir);

long ccsd_trpdrv(double * __restrict__ f1n, double * __restrict__ f1t,
                 double * __restrict__ f2n, double * __restrict__ f2t,
                 double * __restrict__ f3n, double * __restrict__ f3t,
                 double * __restrict__ f4n, double * __restrict__ f4t,
                 double * __restrict__ eorb,
                 int    * __restrict__ ncor_, int * __restrict__ nocc_, int * __restrict__ nvir_,
                 double * __restrict__ emp4_, double * __restrict__ emp5_,
                 int    * __restrict__ a_, int * __restrict__ i_, int * __restrict__ j_, int * __restrict__ k_, int * __restrict__ klo_,
                 double * __restrict__ tij, double * __restrict__ tkj, double * __restrict__ tia, double * __restrict__ tka,
                 double * __restrict__ xia, double * __restrict__ xka, double * __restrict__ jia, double * __restrict__ jka,
                 double * __restrict__ kia, double * __restrict__ kka, double * __restrict__ jij, double * __restrict__ jkj,
                 double * __restrict__ kij, double * __restrict__ kkj,
                 double * __restrict__ dintc1, double * __restrict__ dintx1, double * __restrict__ t1v1,
                 double * __restrict__ dintc2, double * __restrict__ dintx2, double * __restrict__ t1v2)
{
    double emp4 = *emp4_;
    double emp5 = *emp5_;

    double emp4i = 0.0;
    double emp5i = 0.0;
    double emp4k = 0.0;
    double emp5k = 0.0;

    const int ncor = *ncor_;
    const int nocc = *nocc_;
    const int nvir = *nvir_;

    /* convert from Fortran to C offset convention... */
    const int k   = *k_ - 1;
    //const int klo = *klo_ - 1;
    const int a   = *a_ - 1;
    const int i   = *i_ - 1;
    const int j   = *j_ - 1;

    const double eaijk = eorb[a] - (eorb[ncor+i] + eorb[ncor+j] + eorb[ncor+k]);

    long time = ccsd_tengy_gpu(f1n, f1t, f2n, f2t, f3n, f3t, f4n, f4t,
                               dintc1, dintx1, t1v1, dintc2, dintx2, t1v2,
                               eorb, eaijk, &emp4i, &emp5i, &emp4k, &emp5k,
                               ncor, nocc, nvir);

    emp4 += emp4i;
    emp5 += emp5i;

    if (*i_ != *k_) {
        emp4 += emp4k;
        emp5 += emp5k;
    }

    *emp4_ = emp4;
    *emp5_ = emp5;

    return time;
}

void kernel_ref (const double * __restrict__ f1n,    const double * __restrict__ f1t,
                 const double * __restrict__ f2n,    const double * __restrict__ f2t,
                 const double * __restrict__ f3n,    const double * __restrict__ f3t,
                 const double * __restrict__ f4n,    const double * __restrict__ f4t,
                 const double * __restrict__ dintc1, const double * __restrict__ dintx1, const double * __restrict__ t1v1,
                 const double * __restrict__ dintc2, const double * __restrict__ dintx2, const double * __restrict__ t1v2,
                 const double * __restrict__ eorb,   const double eaijk,
                 double &emp4i, double &emp5i,
                 double &emp4k, double &emp5k,
                 const int ncor, const int nocc, const int nvir)
{
  for (int c = 0; c < nvir; c++) {
    for (int b = 0; b < nvir; b++) {
      const double denom = -1.0 / (eorb[ncor+nocc+b] + eorb[ncor+nocc+c] + eaijk);

      // nvir < 10000 so this should never overflow
      const int bc = b+c*nvir;
      const int cb = c+b*nvir;

      const double f1nbc = f1n[bc];
      const double f1tbc = f1t[bc];
      const double f1ncb = f1n[cb];
      const double f1tcb = f1t[cb];

      const double f2nbc = f2n[bc];
      const double f2tbc = f2t[bc];
      const double f2ncb = f2n[cb];
      const double f2tcb = f2t[cb];

      const double f3nbc = f3n[bc];
      const double f3tbc = f3t[bc];
      const double f3ncb = f3n[cb];
      const double f3tcb = f3t[cb];

      const double f4nbc = f4n[bc];
      const double f4tbc = f4t[bc];
      const double f4ncb = f4n[cb];
      const double f4tcb = f4t[cb];

      emp4i += denom * (f1tbc+f1ncb+f2tcb+f3nbc+f4ncb) * (f1tbc-f2tbc*2-f3tbc*2+f4tbc)
                        - denom * (f1nbc+f1tcb+f2ncb+f3ncb) * (f1tbc*2-f2tbc-f3tbc+f4tbc*2)
                        + denom * 3 * (f1nbc*(f1nbc+f3ncb+f4tcb*2) +f2nbc*f2tcb+f3nbc*f4tbc);

      emp4k += denom * (f1nbc+f1tcb+f2ncb+f3tbc+f4tcb) * (f1nbc-f2nbc*2-f3nbc*2+f4nbc)
                        - denom * (f1tbc+f1ncb+f2tcb+f3tcb) * (f1nbc*2-f2nbc-f3nbc+f4nbc*2)
                        + denom * 3 * (f1tbc*(f1tbc+f3tcb+f4ncb*2) +f2tbc*f2ncb+f3tbc*f4nbc);

      const double t1v1b = t1v1[b];
      const double t1v2b = t1v2[b];

      const double dintx1c = dintx1[c];
      const double dintx2c = dintx2[c];
      const double dintc1c = dintc1[c];
      const double dintc2c = dintc2[c];

      emp5i += denom * t1v1b * dintx1c * (f1tbc+f2nbc+f4ncb-(f3tbc+f4nbc+f2ncb+f1nbc+f2tbc+f3ncb)*2
                       +(f3nbc+f4tbc+f1ncb)*4)
                       + denom * t1v1b * dintc1c * (f1nbc+f4nbc+f1tcb -(f2nbc+f3nbc+f2tcb)*2);
      emp5k += denom * t1v2b * dintx2c * (f1nbc+f2tbc+f4tcb -(f3nbc+f4tbc+f2tcb +f1tbc+f2nbc+f3tcb)*2
                       +(f3tbc+f4nbc+f1tcb)*4)
                       + denom * t1v2b * dintc2c * (f1tbc+f4tbc+f1ncb -(f2tbc+f3tbc+f2ncb)*2);
    }
  }
}

void ccsd_tengy_ref(const double * __restrict__ f1n,    const double * __restrict__ f1t,
                    const double * __restrict__ f2n,    const double * __restrict__ f2t,
                    const double * __restrict__ f3n,    const double * __restrict__ f3t,
                    const double * __restrict__ f4n,    const double * __restrict__ f4t,
                    const double * __restrict__ dintc1, const double * __restrict__ dintx1, const double * __restrict__ t1v1,
                    const double * __restrict__ dintc2, const double * __restrict__ dintx2, const double * __restrict__ t1v2,
                    const double * __restrict__ eorb,   const double eaijk,
                    double &emp4i_, double &emp5i_,
                    double &emp4k_, double &emp5k_,
                    const int ncor, const int nocc, const int nvir)
{
  double emp5i = 0.0, emp4i = 0.0, emp5k = 0.0, emp4k = 0.0;

  kernel_ref(
        f1n,
        f1t,
        f2n,
        f2t,
        f3n,
        f3t,
        f4n,
        f4t,
        dintc1,
        dintx1,
        t1v1,
        dintc2,
        dintx2,
        t1v2,
        eorb, 
        eaijk,
        emp4i, 
        emp5i, 
        emp4k,
        emp5k, 
        ncor, nocc, nvir);

  emp4i_ = emp4i;
  emp4k_ = emp4k;
  emp5i_ = emp5i;
  emp5k_ = emp5k;
}

void ccsd_trpdrv_ref(double * __restrict__ f1n, double * __restrict__ f1t,
                     double * __restrict__ f2n, double * __restrict__ f2t,
                     double * __restrict__ f3n, double * __restrict__ f3t,
                     double * __restrict__ f4n, double * __restrict__ f4t,
                     double * __restrict__ eorb,
                     int    * __restrict__ ncor_, int * __restrict__ nocc_, int * __restrict__ nvir_,
                     double * __restrict__ emp4_, double * __restrict__ emp5_,
                     int    * __restrict__ a_, int * __restrict__ i_, int * __restrict__ j_, int * __restrict__ k_, int * __restrict__ klo_,
                     double * __restrict__ tij, double * __restrict__ tkj, double * __restrict__ tia, double * __restrict__ tka,
                     double * __restrict__ xia, double * __restrict__ xka, double * __restrict__ jia, double * __restrict__ jka,
                     double * __restrict__ kia, double * __restrict__ kka, double * __restrict__ jij, double * __restrict__ jkj,
                     double * __restrict__ kij, double * __restrict__ kkj,
                     double * __restrict__ dintc1, double * __restrict__ dintx1, double * __restrict__ t1v1,
                     double * __restrict__ dintc2, double * __restrict__ dintx2, double * __restrict__ t1v2)
{
    double emp4 = *emp4_;
    double emp5 = *emp5_;

    double emp4i = 0.0;
    double emp5i = 0.0;
    double emp4k = 0.0;
    double emp5k = 0.0;

    const int ncor = *ncor_;
    const int nocc = *nocc_;
    const int nvir = *nvir_;

    /* convert from Fortran to C offset convention... */
    const int k   = *k_ - 1;
    //const int klo = *klo_ - 1;
    const int a   = *a_ - 1;
    const int i   = *i_ - 1;
    const int j   = *j_ - 1;

    const double eaijk = eorb[a] - (eorb[ncor+i] + eorb[ncor+j] + eorb[ncor+k]);

    ccsd_tengy_ref(f1n, f1t, f2n, f2t, f3n, f3t, f4n, f4t,
                   dintc1, dintx1, t1v1, dintc2, dintx2, t1v2,
                   eorb, eaijk, emp4i, emp5i, emp4k, emp5k,
                   ncor, nocc, nvir);

    emp4 += emp4i;
    emp5 += emp5i;

    if (*i_ != *k_) {
        emp4 += emp4k;
        emp5 += emp5k;
    }

    *emp4_ = emp4;
    *emp5_ = emp5;
}

prediction.blockSz_explanation: From the source: block = dim3(BLOCK_SIZE, BLOCK_SIZE) = dim3(16, 16). So blockSz = (16, 16, 1).
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: Looking at the SASS, there is one FSETP.GEU instruction at 0x1e0 which is a FP32 comparison used in the denom computation path. This executes once per active thread (40000 threads). However, FSETP is a comparison/predicate-setting instruction, not an arithmetic operation. The FSEL instructions in the reduction are FP32 selects (conditional moves), not arithmetic. There are no FP32 arithmetic instructions (FADD, FMUL, FFMA) in the kernel. So FP32 FLOP count is 0.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation:
Per active thread (b < 200 && c < 200), the kernel computes:
1) denom computation: 2 DADD (eorb[b]+eorb[c], +eaijk) + 1 RCP64 (division). The RCP64 in SASS uses MUFU.RCP64H + 4 DFMA + some helper work. Counting from SASS main path: MUFU.RCP64H(1) + DFMA at 0x1f0,0x200,0x210,0x220,0x230 = 5 DFMA. That's 1 MUFU + 5 DFMA = 11 FP64 ops (each DFMA = 2 FLOPs). Plus 2 DADD = 2. Total for denom: 2 + 1 + 10 = 13.

2) Main computation (s1, s2, s3, s4): Counting DADD, DFMA, DMUL instructions in the main body from SASS (addresses 0x1a0 through 0x0bb0):
- DADD instructions: at 0x1a0, 0x1b0, 0x4a0, 0x4b0, 0x4c0, 0x4d0, 0x4e0, 0x4f0, 0x530, 0x540, 0x550, 0x560, 0x570, 0x580, 0x590, 0x5a0, 0x5b0, 0x5c0, 0x5d0, 0x5e0, 0x5f0, 0x660, 0x670, 0x680, 0x6f0, 0x700, 0x730, 0x760, 0x830, 0x840, 0x850, 0x860, 0x870, 0x880, 0x890, 0x8b0, 0x8e0, 0x900, 0x9a0, 0x9b0, 0x9c0, 0x9d0, 0x9e0, 0x9f0, 0xa00, 0xa10, 0xa20, 0xa30, 0xa40, 0xa50, 0xa60, 0xa70, 0xa80, 0xa90, 0xaa0, 0xab0, 0xac0, 0xad0, 0xae0, 0xaf0 = 60 DADD (each 1 FLOP)
- DFMA instructions: at 0x500, 0x610, 0x6a0, 0x6b0, 0x750, 0x770, 0x790, 0x7b0, 0x7c0, 0x7e0, 0x800, 0x810, 0x820, 0xb00, 0xb10, 0xba0, 0xbb0 = 17 DFMA (each 2 FLOPs = 34)
- DMUL instructions: at 0x510, 0x530(no, that's DADD), let me recount: 0x510, 0x600, 0x6b0(no DFMA), 0x6c0, 0x740, 0x7a0, 0xb20, 0xb30, 0xb40, 0xb50, 0xb60, 0xb70, 0xb80, 0xb90 = 14 DMUL (each 1 FLOP)

Total per active thread: 13 (denom) + 60 (DADD) + 34 (DFMA) + 14 (DMUL) = 121 FP64 ops.

Then the block reduction for 4 values (s1-s4): Each reduction uses warp-level shuffles with DADD. For BLOCK_SIZE=16x16=256 threads, CUB BlockReduce with WARP_REDUCTIONS: 8 warps, each does 5 warp-level DADD steps (for 32 lanes) = 5 DADDs per warp per reduction. Then the first warp combines 8 partial sums with 7 DADDs. Total per reduction: 8*5 + 7 = 47 DADDs. For 4 reductions: 4*47 = 188 DADDs.

But looking at SASS more carefully, the reduction path has two code paths (fast SHFL path and slow __cuda_sm70_shflsync_down_p path). The fast path threads (warp size ≤ 32 with all active) use inline SHFL+DADD. The slow path calls the helper. For 200x200 active threads in 13x13 blocks of 16x16, most warps are fully active. Let me count reduction DADDs from SASS: For each of the 4 reductions, there are 5 DADD steps in warp reduction + up to 7 DADDs in cross-warp reduction (for thread 0 only). Per block: 256 threads * 5 DADDs (warp level, but only meaningful for active lanes) + 7 DADDs (thread 0). Across all 169 blocks, 4 reductions each.

Actually, for the reduction, each warp does 5 shuffle-down + DADD steps (all 32 threads participate but only some produce meaningful results). Each DADD executes on all threads in the warp. So per warp: 5 DADDs * 32 threads = 160 DADDs. 8 warps per block = 1280 DADDs. Then cross-warp: 7 DADDs for 1 thread. Per reduction: 1280 + 7 = 1287. For 4 reductions: 5148 per block. Plus 4 atomicAdd DADDs for thread (0,0).

Total active threads for main body: 200*200 = 40000. But launched threads = 208*208 = 43264. Inactive threads (3264) still participate in reductions with s1=s2=s3=s4=0.

FP64 FLOPs = 40000 * 121 (main body) + 169 blocks * (4 reductions * (8 warps * 5 DADDs * 32 threads + 7 DADDs * 1 thread)) + 169 * 4 (atomicAdd) = 4,840,000 + 169 * (4 * (1280 + 7)) + 676 = 4,840,000 + 169 * 5148 + 676 = 4,840,000 + 870,012 + 676 = 5,710,688.

Wait, I need to be more careful. The SHFL+DADD pattern: each thread in the warp executes the DADD regardless. So 5 DADDs per thread per warp-level reduction, times 32 threads per warp, times 8 warps = 5*256 = 1280 per block per reduction. Cross-warp: only thread with P1=false (threadIdx.x==0 && threadIdx.y==0) does 7 DADDs. So per reduction per block: 1280 + 7 = 1287. 4 reductions: 5148. 169 blocks: 870,012. Plus 4 atomic DADDs per block: 676. Grand total: 4,840,000 + 870,012 + 676 = 5,710,688.

prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation:
The kernel reads from 15 arrays. For active threads (b < 200, c < 200):
- eorb: 2 reads per thread at indices ncor+nocc+b and ncor+nocc+c. With ncor=0, nocc=200, nvir=200, these access eorb[200..399]. Unique footprint: 200 doubles = 1600 bytes. Fits in cache.
- f1n, f1t, f2n, f2t, f3n, f3t, f4n, f4t: each read at indices bc and cb. Each array is 200*200=40000 doubles = 320000 bytes. Unique footprint per array: 40000*8 = 320000 bytes. 8 arrays * 320000 = 2,560,000 bytes.
- dintc1, dintc2, dintx1, dintx2: each read at index c (0..199). 200 doubles each = 1600 bytes each. 4 * 1600 = 6400 bytes.
- t1v1, t1v2: each read at index b (0..199). 200 doubles each = 1600 bytes each. 2 * 1600 = 3200 bytes.
- emp4i, emp5i, emp4k, emp5k: 4 atomicAdd reads, 4 * 8 = 32 bytes.

Total unique read footprint: 2,560,000 + 1,600 + 6,400 + 3,200 + 32 = 2,571,232 bytes.

The L2 cache is 6 MB. The total unique footprint (~2.57 MB) fits in L2. So DRAM reads ≈ unique footprint (compulsory misses) = 2,571,232 bytes. Rounding to cache line granularity (128 bytes): the 8 large arrays each have 40000*8/128 = 2500 cache lines = 320000 bytes. The small arrays and eorb add a few more cache lines. Total ≈ 8*320000 + ceil(1600/128)*128*7 + 32 ≈ 2,560,000 + 13*128*7 + 128 = 2,560,000 + 11,648 + 128 ≈ 2,571,776 bytes.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: The kernel writes only via 4 atomicAdd operations per block (169 blocks), writing to 4 double values (emp4i, emp5i, emp4k, emp5k). That's 4 * 8 = 32 bytes of unique write footprint. This easily fits in L2 cache (6 MB), so no DRAM writes occur during this kernel invocation. The dirty cache lines remain in L2 until evicted by a later operation.

prediction.gridSz_explanation: From main(), the first call to ccsd_trpdrv occurs at klo=1, j=1, i=1, k=1 with command-line args nocc=200 and nvir=200. In ccsd_tengy_gpu the kernel is launched as dim3((nvir+15)/16,(nvir+15)/16) with BLOCK_SIZE=16, so the first invocation uses grid=(13,13,1).
prediction.blockSz_explanation: BLOCK_SIZE is a compile-time macro equal to 16 in ccsd_tengy.cu, and the launch uses dim3(BLOCK_SIZE,BLOCK_SIZE). Therefore each block has 16x16x1 = 256 threads.
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: The kernel source and SASS show only double-precision arithmetic for the main computation plus integer/address ops and shuffle/control logic; there are no FP32 arithmetic instructions on the taken path. Therefore the FP32 FLOP count for the first invocation is zero.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: For each active thread (b<200,c<200), source-level counting gives: denom computation = 3 adds + 1 reciprocal/division + 1 unary negation = 5 FLOPs; s1 = 24 adds/subs + 14 muls = 38; s2 = 24 + 14 = 38; s3 = 16 adds/subs + 14 muls = 30; s4 = 16 + 14 = 30, totaling 141 FP64 FLOPs per active thread. The launch creates 13*13*16*16 = 43264 threads but only 200*200 = 40000 satisfy the bounds, so thread-body work is 141*40000 = 5,640,000 FP64 FLOPs; BlockReduce then sums four scalars over 256 threads in each of 169 blocks, which with CUB warp reductions corresponds to 255 additions per reduction, i.e. 4*255*169 = 172,380 more FP64 adds; finally one thread per block performs four FP64 atomicAdd operations, counted as 4 FP64 additions per block = 676.
